title: Supervise continuous execution with admission, semantic progress and cancellation
summary: Continuous mode may remove implicit global ceilings only when each step remains admitted and meaningful progress is observable; explicit budgets, limits and cancellation still win.
reusable_steps: Continuous mode may remove implicit global ceilings only when each step remains admitted and meaningful progress is observable; explicit budgets, limits and cancellation still win
expected_outcome: Separate the lifetime of a continuous goal from the finite deadlines of individual model, tool and compaction operations. Remove an implicit turn ceiling only when the real caller supplies per-step admission. Continuous delegation requires a harness that reports semantic progress; process liveness and increasing stdout do not renew an inactivity window. Unsupported providers remain bounded and must refuse an explicit unsupported continuous request. Preserve explicit max-turn, budget and deadline settings; late results after cancellation or terminal state must not revive success. Detect repeated operations using both arguments and results so legitimate progress and polling are not treated as a stall. Fence compaction by generation and preserve raw scoped history before incomplete recovery; do not replay uncertain external effects. Bound child-result presentation using the parent's latest prompt occupancy, not cumulative session tokens, while preserving full scoped artifacts and valid structured results. Classify model-specific rate limits separately from provider-wide authentication failure so one model's cooldown does not disable healthy siblings. Fake-provider and virtual-time regressions do not establish paid-provider or long-duration production performance.
